topic: What if Oden never adopted the dream of opening Wano's borders after Laugh Tale
title: What If Oden Never Opened Wano's Borders?
description: Oden never actually opened Wano's borders -- he fell before he even became shogun. But what if he never even dreamed of it at all? Change one decision in chapter 968 and the dream Yamato inherits, the reason he defies Kaidou, and the choice Momonosuke makes after the war all break differently. This is the quiet ending nobody predicted.
comment: Was Oden's dream always bigger than Wano itself, or did Yamato just need something of his father's to believe in? Pick one.

lines.text: So the ending barely moves. What disappears is the entire reason it was ever a question worth asking.

lines.text: Take away the one man who ever wanted that watching to mean something, and the silence turns permanent.

lines.text: Not a fearful pause before some future chapter. An ending with nobody left to argue against it.

lines.text: Oden spent his whole life feeling confined by Wano's borders.

shot.fallback: young samurai staring past a border wall

lines.text: He tried thirty-eight separate times to sail past them before he even turned eighteen.

lines.text: Some fans will say Momonosuke would open the borders eventually anyway, dream or no dream.

shot.fallback: young ruler considering a difficult decision

lines.text: Maybe. But chapter 1041 shows a shogun who needed his father's conviction just to feel like a coward about saying no.

shot.fallback: young ruler burdened by an absent conviction

lines.text: Take that conviction out of the logbook, and there's nothing left to even feel guilty about.

shot.fallback: young ruler feeling strangely at peace with isolation

lines.text: Guilt is actually the useful part here, because guilt is what keeps a question alive for later.

shot.fallback: young ruler lingering on an unresolved question

lines.text: A shogun who feels nothing about staying closed has no reason to ever revisit the choice.

shot.fallback: young ruler settling comfortably into isolation

lines.text: Kin'emon spent twenty years promising Toki he'd finish Oden's work, whatever that work turned out to be.

shot.fallback: loyal retainer making a solemn promise

lines.text: In canon, that promise points outward, toward the rest of the world.

shot.fallback: retainer looking toward a distant horizon

lines.text: In mine, it just points back inside, toward keeping the people already here safe.

shot.fallback: retainer standing protectively over his homeland

lines.text: Both versions honor Oden. Only one of them ever lets Wano's name reach the rest of the world.

lines.text: Yamato still leaves with Luffy's crew, telling himself he's carrying Oden's spirit out to sea at last.

lines.text: He's right about the spirit. He's just wrong about the one thing he thinks he's finishing.

shot.fallback: warrior sailing away, unaware of what's missing

lines.text: There's no unfinished dream left behind in Wano for him to ever come back and complete.

shot.fallback: quiet, settled homeland with nothing left pending

lines.text: He just gets to be free, which was always the one thing Oden actually wanted for him too.

shot.fallback: warrior finally free, sailing toward open water

lines.text: Freedom for one son instead of an open country for everyone else left behind is still a brutal trade.

lines.text: I think that's a worse ending than losing the fight, because nobody even notices it happened.

lines.text: So, does one erased page in chapter 968 really decide Wano's whole future? Tell me which side you're on.
